headline: Indian benchmarks log worst month since March as global headwinds and rising oil prices weigh on sentiment

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Rising crude oil prices and global rate hike bets sparked significant outflows from benchmark shares
Persistent FII outflows and global headwinds pressured Indian markets throughout September
US stock futures edged lower as investors awaited a key inflation report
India's bond yields reached over two-year lows as expectations for interest rate hikes increased
whatHappening: Indian benchmark indices logged their worst monthly performance since March and worst nine-month show in 15 years
Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (MRPL) cancelled fuel export tenders following a fire at its site
The Union Cabinet approved a hike in Rabi minimum support prices for the 2027-28 season
The Nifty 50 closed at 22,620 while the Sensex ended the day nearly flat amid high volatility
summary: Indian markets concluded September on a weak note, marking the worst monthly performance since March due to global rate hike fears and high oil prices. The Sensex and Nifty also recorded their poorest nine-month showing in 15 years amid persistent FII outflows. Corporate activity saw MRPL cancelling export tenders following a fire at its facility.
